headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Aci’s broad egress and CRM/email access can feed OpenMetadata’s MCP/API workflows with sensitive context unless tightly isolated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aci can use direct function calls or an MCP server, and OpenMetadata exposes MCP tools/APIs/webhooks. That shared channel makes instruction-like content in one agent’s outputs plausibly consumable by the other. No provenance or isolation mechanism is documented, so the interaction is inferred from both profiles.
conditions: IF Aci forwards OpenMetadata-generated text into an MCP tool call without sanitization, prompt injection becomes actionable.
IF OpenMetadata ingests Aci-produced content as trusted metadata or instructions, the bridge is exploitable.
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of agent outputs as instructions.
Insert a human review step before any MCP tool call that contains free-form text.
Restrict MCP tools to allowlisted schemas only.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents onto separate workspaces or queues.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress; OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data and can act through APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks. If they share a workspace or exchange context, sensitive business data can flow out through Aci’s egress or into OpenMetadata’s cataloging surfaces.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or message bus, sensitive CRM/email content can be copied into governance metadata.
IF Aci sends its context to external APIs while holding customer data, leakage can occur through its default egress path.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces.
Block outbound network access except to approved endpoints.
Redact CRM/email fields before passing content to OpenMetadata.
Review webhook payloads for sensitive fields before enabling them.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both can write to mutable external systems: Aci via CRM/email/calendar/Sheets/Notion-style APIs, OpenMetadata via APIs/SDKs/events/webhooks. Overlapping writes to shared resources can race or overwrite state, though the profiles do not prove unrestricted filesystem writes or git mutation.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same CRM record, sheet, or webhook target without locking, last-write-wins conflicts can occur.
IF orchestration fans out concurrent jobs to both agents on the same object, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Serialize writes to shared records.
Assign one agent as the sole writer per resource.
Use idempotency keys for all external mutations.
Add optimistic concurrency checks where supported.
requires-engineering: introduce a lock or lease service.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and OpenMetadata can consume events, APIs, and webhooks. If OpenMetadata treats Aci’s outputs as authoritative, an error in Aci can propagate into catalog, lineage, or governance records. The reverse path is also plausible, but neither profile documents built-in verification between them.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests Aci-produced facts without validation, incorrect metadata can cascade downstream.
IF Aci acts on OpenMetadata-derived metadata as if it were ground truth, bad lineage or governance data can trigger wrong actions.
mitigations: Require a verification step before acting on either agent’s output.
Compare outputs against source-of-truth systems before writeback.
Limit automated actions to low-risk drafts only.
Log and review discrepancies between agents.
requires-engineering: add schema and provenance validation between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Aci explicitly touches email, CRM, support, and calendar data and handles OAuth/secrets; OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge and is verified open-source with API/webhook surfaces. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed through OpenMetadata without matching retention controls, policy mismatch occurs.
IF Aci processes email or CRM data under stricter residency rules than OpenMetadata’s deployment, compliance breach risk increases.
mitigations: Classify the data before routing it between agents.
Disable retention-heavy logging for regulated fields.
Confirm residency and DPA terms for every external endpoint.
Restrict regulated data to one agent only.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a shared retention policy.
